items.prompt: Given the root of a binary tree, return its node values grouped by level: [[level 0], [level 1], …], left to right.
items.why: 'Grouped by level' → a queue, with the level size frozen at the start of each round. DFS can do it by passing the depth, but the level order is BFS's natural output.

items.prompt: Given a binary tree, return the number of nodes on the shortest path from the root down to the nearest leaf.
items.why: The nearest leaf → BFS, which can stop at the first leaf it pops. DFS has to explore the whole tree to be sure no shallower leaf exists.

items.prompt: Given a binary tree and a target, return true if some root-to-leaf path adds up to the target.
items.why: Root-to-leaf paths → DFS, passing the remaining sum down the recursion. Levels don't help, and there are no overlapping subproblems for DP.

items.prompt: Given a begin word, an end word and a dictionary, return the fewest one-letter changes needed to turn the begin word into the end word, where every intermediate word is in the dictionary.
items.why: Fewest steps where every step costs 1 → BFS on an implicit graph (words are nodes, one-letter changes are edges). Backtracking or DFS would explore every sequence.

items.prompt: There are n courses and a list of pairs [a, b] meaning b must be taken before a. Return an order in which all courses can be taken, or [] if that is impossible.
items.why: Prerequisites and an order that respects them → topological sort (Kahn's in-degree queue, or DFS post-order). The deciding signal is the dependency order, not distance.

items.prompt: A network has n nodes and directed edges with travel times. A signal starts at node k. Return how long it takes for every node to receive it.
items.why: Edges have different travel times → Dijkstra with a min-heap. Plain BFS counts edges, not time, so it's only right when every edge costs the same.

items.prompt: Return the length of the longest path between any two nodes of a binary tree (the path may not pass through the root).
items.why: Each node needs the heights of both subtrees first → post-order DFS that returns a height and records the best left + right. BFS can't combine children's answers.

items.prompt: In an n × n grid of 0s and 1s, return the length of the shortest path of 0-cells from the top-left to the bottom-right, moving in 8 directions, or -1.
items.why: Shortest path, unit-cost moves → BFS from the start, counting rings. It's on a grid, but the question is a distance, not regions (islands). Moves go in all directions, so there's no DP order.
